_readme: THE APPLY ORDER OF supabase/migrations/**. This is the single source of truth
for rebuilding the database from the repo, and it is verified on every push by
tests/schema-drift.mjs (via tests/schema-replay.mjs).
WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. Filename order does NOT replay. Measured
2026-08-14: applying supabase/schema.sql + every migration in filename order
gets 23 of 41 files in and fails the other 18. Two reasons, both structural:
1. '2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql' sorts BEFORE '2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql',
because '-' (0x2D) < '.' (0x2E). The -2 file's first act is to check that
clan_board exists and raise if it does not, so it fails first, every time.
2. Nine files are dated 2026-08-11 and alphabetical order puts 'accrual',
'accrue-gate', 'anon-execute-lockdown', 'apply-engine' and
'authenticated-surface-lockdown' all BEFORE 'player-state' â€” which is the
foundation every one of them depends on. There is no naming scheme that
rescues this after the fact.
Before this file, the working order existed only as a hand-maintained const
array inside tests/pglite-chain.mjs and another inside
tests/conservation-fuzz.mjs, each covering a DIFFERENT SUBSET of the
migrations, and neither one covering all of them. That means the order
required to rebuild the database was not written down anywhere.
RULES:
Â· Every .sql file in supabase/migrations/ must appear exactly once, across
'pre_schema', 'order' and 'excluded'. The guard FAILS on a file that is in
none of them â€” so a new migration cannot be silently left out of the
rebuild. The full apply sequence is: pre_schema, then supabase/schema.sql,
then order.
Â· A new migration goes where it actually has to run, not where its date
puts it.
Â· 'excluded' is a claim that a rebuilt database is CORRECT without the file.
Never add one to make the chain go green.

_why: GUCs production was actually applied with, not shortcuts.
it, and production was applied with it set on 2026-08-13 (that is what closed
A11). A rebuild that omitted it would leave beta_invites world-readable and
the file would tell you so, loudly.
market_wipe_ok: read by 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql, which is in 'order'
(staged; it supersedes and deletes the old 2026-08-11-market-v2.sql). The
GUC gates that file's DROP...CASCADE of the live market tables.

_pre_schema_why: supabase/schema.sql creates game_saves and game_events with `create table if
not exists` as a bootstrap fallback, and its own header says they are assumed
to already exist. Those fallback definitions do not match production: different
primary key on game_saves, different COLUMN NAMES on game_events (kind vs
event_type, created_at vs occurred_at). Running the true shapes first makes
schema.sql's fallback no-op on a rebuild exactly as it no-ops on production.
The alternative â€” ALTER + rename the columns afterwards â€” is a rename on the
table holding every player's save, which cannot be rolled forward past a
failure. Ordering is reversible; that is not.

_order_notes.2026-09-09-import-apply-slot-entitlement: STAGED, NOT APPLIED - REVIEW ONLY; the Coordinator applies AFTER a Security GO. _order_notes.2026-09-08-hero-slot-buy.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED - REVIEW ONLY; the Coordinator applies. Closes the two live hero-slot defects the play-gate found on production, plus a third and larger one found while building it. (1) THE BUY BUTTON IS LIT AND DEAD: public.hr_unlock_offers carries all four character_slot rows with refusal='namespace_unsupported:character_slot' and gold=null, because a hero slot is priced in GEMS and that generated catalogue has a gold column and no other - so hr_unlock_buy refuses the namespace by construction and the click dead-ends through a confirm modal with no visible outcome. The only other path, src/multi-character.js unlockSlot(), is a client-side `G.gems -= cost`, and gems are SERVER-OF-RECORD and ARMED (src/net/record.js SERVER_OF_RECORD carries `gems` with no dormant gate), so that debit is reconciled away by the next envelope. (2) OWNERSHIP IS CLIENT-AUTHORED in the G.heroSlotsUnlocked residue - the b371 gem dupe that multi-character.js's own header documents ('a cloud restore reverted the gems debit and KEPT the slot - the purchase became free') and whose closing paragraph names this exact verb as the fix. (3) THE ONE FOUND HERE, AND THE BIGGEST: hr_create_character(p_slot) is granted to `authenticated` and has only ever validated p_slot for SHAPE ('if v_slot < 0 or v_slot > 5 then bad_slot'), so POST /rpc/hr_create_character {"p_slot":4} from any signed-in console mints a fifth character with a full starting kit - 500 gold, a Bronze Sword, farm plots, the free Auto-Eat I - for nothing, five times over. That is the entire 3,100-gem ladder bypassed by one fetch, and it would also LAUNDER into a permanent entitlement through this file's own grandfather clause. A price is not a price if the thing can be taken without paying it, so the gate is not scope creep; it is the other half of the same property and lands in the same transaction. WHAT IT ADDS: public.hr_hero_slots (slot_id 1-4, cost_gems, premium_waived; RLS on, no policy, every client grant revoked), public.hr_hero_slots_of(uuid) - the ONE ownership predicate, read by three callers so a grandfather clause cannot have three spellings - and hr_buy_hero_slot__ungated(int,int,uuid) behind a rate-gated authenticated-only wrapper. THE ACCOUNT/CHARACTER SPLIT IS THE DESIGN DECISION: the MONEY comes from the CALLING character's player_state row (the wallet the topbar gem chip is showing - measured on production, the one two-character account holds 527 gems on slot 0 and 0 on slot 1, so charging any other row would take gems the player cannot see and quote a shortfall that is not on their screen), while the ENTITLEMENT is written to the account's canonical row, SLOT 0, and read account-wide (player_progress has no account-level home and an FK onto player_state; filing it under the calling slot would make a slot bought on Hero 2 invisible from Hero 1). Two advisory locks in canonical order - slot 0's key FIRST, byte-identical to hr_apply's - because a per-character lock alone would let two characters of one account buy the same slot at once and both charge. THERE IS NO FREE PATH IN THE VERB: the Hearth Hall waiver moves out of device-local localStorage (one devtools line = three free slots today) and becomes a fact about OWNERSHIP, so a waived slot answers already_owned and never runs a zero-gem grant; the migration's own gate asserts the single grant is downstream of the single debit. Refuses by name: bad_slot / unknown_slot / requires_previous_slot / already_owned / insufficient_gems / no_character / no_account / hero_slot_daily_cap / rate_limited, plus slot_not_owned from the create gate (which src/net/character.js already routes through its `default: refused` branch, so no client change is needed for it to fail safely). MUST RUN AFTER 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql - the body calls hr_intent_replay from birth rather than being retro-patched, because player_intents is ONE key namespace for every verb - and AFTER 2026-09-04-auto-eat-at-creation.sql, which is the hr_create_character body Sec 8 anchors into. PATCHES THREE LIVE-HASH-TRACKED BODIES PROGRAMMATICALLY (never a restatement - the b484-b487 wave): hr_state_of gains an additive ACCOUNT-scoped `hero_slots` projection at the total_level anchor, hr_rpc_gate gains one bucket at the case terminator, hr_create_character gains the entitlement gate at its fast-path anchor. So after applying, run  node tests/live-hash-drift.mjs --live --write  and let the baseline diff be the deploy record. GRANDFATHERING IS LOAD-BEARING AND MEASURED: production carries ZERO character_slot flag rows and one account (0a47ba77) with characters on slots 0 AND 1, so hr_hero_slots_of counts an existing player_state row as ownership - without that clause the projection would evict a real player's second hero on its first envelope. The clause is safe going forward precisely because Sec 8 makes a row above slot 0 impossible to create without owning the slot. COST AT 100x PLAYERS: four slots exist and each is once-per-ACCOUNT forever, so the lifetime ceiling is 4 player_progress + 4 player_ledger + 4 player_intents rows per account - under 7,200 rows at 600 players, FOREVER, and realistically two orders of magnitude less. hr_hero_slots_of is two index lookups plus a four-row catalogue scan, called once per hr_state_of. REVERSIBLE: drop the two functions and the table, then re-apply 2026-08-23-trait-buy.sql (restores hr_state_of without the projection) and 2026-09-04-auto-eat-at-creation.sql (restores hr_create_character) - WHICH RE-OPENS THE FREE-CHARACTER MINT. Do not revert Sec 8 alone to unblock something. NO EDGE REDEPLOY. Guard: tests/hero-slot-buy.mjs, wired into tests/run-smoke.mjs - a full PGlite chain replay driving a real player through the real rate-gated RPC, plus a THREE-WAY price bind (the authored SLOT_COSTS_GEMS array in src/multi-character.js, the generated src/data/shops.js offers, and public.hr_hero_slots) so a price that differs by one gem fails the build by name, plus a mutation catalogue every entry of which must read RED.
_order_notes.2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-escalates.sql: SECURITY CONDITION C2 on the finding-#7 sign-off. hr_record_rejection classifies every code into c_incident (fires on the FIRST occurrence) or c_escalating (promoted to 'incident' at c_escalate_at = 50 in one user/slot/day). 'intent_mismatch' was in NEITHER, so it stayed severity 'normal' forever at any n — and the class fix in 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql makes twelve more RPCs able to emit it. Security's ruling: it has the rate_limited PROFILE, not the incident profile — ONE is a stale retry (a reload mid-gesture, a bfcache restore, a queued request replayed after a slot switch), FIFTY in a day is a signature an honest client cannot produce, because every client site mints a fresh uuid per gesture. c_incident was considered and REJECTED: alarming on the first late retry produces a permanently-alarming detector, which is a muted one. ANCHORED exactly-once patch on the LIVE body (never a restatement — the b484-b487 lesson), idempotent, ACL captured before the replace and asserted byte-identical after (it writes hr_rejections for an ARBITRARY user id, so a client grant is a way to forge another player's abuse record). §0 fails closed without 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql by name. §3 PROVES the behaviour in an HR822-rolled-back block with the control that matters: ONE occurrence must stay 'normal' (a test that only checked the flip would pass identically if the code had been mis-filed into c_incident) and the FIFTIETH must read 'incident'. Zero cost: hr_rejections is already upserted on (user_id, slot, day, code) and pruned at 180 days; this changes a string in a CASE on a write that already happens. Reversible by re-applying the authoring migration or swapping the arrays back.

_order_notes.2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql: P3 (b493/b494 security pass, finding #7) — CLASS FIX. player_intents is ONE key namespace for every verb; hr_apply (apply-engine S6) compares the stored `intent` AND `slot` before serving a cached envelope, and TWELVE other SECURITY DEFINER RPCs read the same cache and compare NEITHER, so a uuid claimed by any verb answers for every verb (self-only: user_id is auth.uid(); not reachable by accident: every client site mints a fresh uuid). AUDIT OF THE FOUR VERBS THE FINDING NAMED: only hr_claim_goal takes a p_idem at all — hr_claim_daily / hr_claim_rank / hr_claim_milestone / hr_claim_quest / hr_claim_bounty have NO idempotency key and are made idempotent by a player_progress state transition instead, which cannot be confused between intents, so they are not touched. THE OTHER ELEVEN were found by asking the database, not by reading the finding. Creates ONE function (hr_intent_replay, SECURITY INVOKER, revoked from all four roles + PUBLIC — it takes a uuid ARGUMENT, so as a DEFINER function it would be an intent-cache read oracle) and PATCHES the twelve bodies programmatically at a guarded exactly-once anchor (the 2026-08-28-client-state.sql idiom), so it carries NO literal create-or-replace and takes over NO last-toucher role; the patch asserts each body's proacl is byte-identical across the replace. The intent expression passed at each site is COPIED FROM THAT BODY'S OWN player_intents insert (verified statement by statement on production 2026-08-30), so every row already in the table was written with the expression the read now compares against and no live retry changes answer. APPLIES LAST on purpose, and the consequence is stated: a LATER migration that restates one of the twelve from a template silently deletes the hardening — pinned by tests/intent-mismatch.mjs, which replays the WHOLE chain (no upTo) and fails the build if any of the twelve reaches the end without the guard. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: written labels are unchanged (so intra-verb key reuse — one uuid for goal A then goal B — still replays A; self-only, and changing a written label would make a retry that crosses the deploy boundary see intent_mismatch for a claim that succeeded), and intent_mismatch is NOT reclassified as an hr_rejections incident (that array is shared with hr_apply; the severity taxonomy is Security's). Reversible by re-applying the twelve authoring migrations + dropping the helper. Security: touches claim idempotency on money verbs — ACK REQUESTED.
_order_notes.2026-09-03-cron-health-generalized.sql: RELIABILITY (b493/b494 pass) — the b319 lesson, generalised. hr_cron_health alarmed on the size of ONE hardcoded table (game_events), i.e. the incident that happened rather than the class: any table can be the next one, and the three signals that would have shown b319 EARLIEST (database growth RATE, per-table row deltas, connection headroom) were not measured at all. Adds public.hr_db_samples (one hourly row: db bytes, connection headroom, and the top-N tables by size/rows — RLS on, no policy, no client grant, self-pruning at 30 days) and rewrites hr_cron_health to alert on (d) database size + 24h growth rate, (e) any table over the size fuse or growing faster than the per-table fuse — which SUBSUMES the old game_events check at the same 100 MB threshold, so nothing is lost, (f) connection headroom against max_connections (measured 60 on this project; docs/design/server-authority.md 2a-ii calls this the first thing that breaks at 10x), and (g) an escalation for a job that has NEVER run and has been known for over 48h — the hr-kill-credit-prune class, which the old body could only ever report as 'info', forever. Keeps (a) failed runs, (b) stale jobs and (c) as a special case of (e). No new schedule: the existing hourly hr-cron-health job calls it. Also prunes maintenance_log / acked maintenance_alerts at 90 days, which nothing did (471 rows and growing since 2026-08-11). Creates one new function (hr_db_sample) revoked from all four roles; hr_cron_health's own ACL is unchanged and re-asserted. Reversible: re-apply 2026-08-11-telemetry-retention.sql and drop the table + helper. Tests: tests/cron-health.mjs (PGlite: the thresholds fire, the growth rate needs two samples, the sample table self-prunes, nothing is client-reachable).
_order_notes.2026-09-02-renown-kill-faucet.sql: R5 (Security, raised during the kill-daily review): a LIVE, PRE-EXISTING renown faucet in the DEPLOYED 2026-08-30-bounty-kill-credit.sql — NOT introduced by 2026-09-01. hr_credit_kills (bounty branch) writes stat/ev:kill_any and stat/ev:kill_monster:<id>, and hr_renown_of SCORES both (0.05/kill; 5/kill for is_boss ids). STRUCTURAL ROOT: hr_bounty_kills reads stat/ev:kill_monster:<target>, the SAME row the bestiary displays and renown scores, so moving renown is a side effect of making a bounty completable. MEASURED: all 108 monsters are bounty-eligible and the 14 bosses are tier 6; at damage level 99 max_hit_ceil is 319, so a 520-HP dragon needs 2 swings -> min_kill 1200ms -> 65 boss kills/min = 19,500 renown/hr, ~8.5x honest, with no gear, no risk and no combat. Re-accepting is NOT needed — one bounty held indefinitely sustains it (re-accepting is worse for the attacker: it resets accepted_at so the cap restarts at 0). WHAT THE SCORE BUYS: the renown BOARD is not the exposure (removed from leaderboard_ranked by 2026-08-18 as no_server_source); the consumers are hr_claim_rank (1,603,000 gold + 925 gems per character across serf..highking; x6 slots = 9,618,000 gold + 5,550 gems; gold feeds the LIVE wealth board and is market purchasing power, gems are premium) and hr_perks_of renownAllXp (+0.04 all-skill XP, feeding the LIVE total_level/combat_level boards). ~6.2h scripted vs ~53h honest to highking. THE FIX (design option C of three, the two rejected recorded in docs/design/renown-kill-faucet.md): DISCOUNT the client-credited portion inside the SCORE rather than capping the writes — a ceiling two orders above the honest rate is a fuse, not a control. hr_credit_kills additionally records ev:kill_credited:<target> and ev:kill_credited_any by the SAME v_applied; hr_renown_of scores greatest(0, counter - credited), per-monster for the boss term (an aggregate discount would let credits on a NON-boss target erase honest boss renown). Client credit therefore contributes EXACTLY ZERO renown. ASYMMETRY BY DESIGN: hr_credit_kills__ungated is PATCHED programmatically at a guarded exactly-once anchor (the combat-style idiom) because it is a WRITE path with money downstream that this file did not author — restating it is how a hotfix gets silently reverted; hr_renown_of is RESTATED because it is stable, writes nothing, is ~60 lines of pure arithmetic, is hr_engine-only, and changes in two terms in its middle. §0b pins the live hr_renown_of body first (md5 beed1fb6221211794ee5853dfb111062, normalised length 2931, MEASURED on BOTH production and a full PGlite replay and found byte-identical) with [[:space:]]+ normalisation, NOT ‘s+’ (the two runtimes disagree on backslash classes under standard_conforming_strings — measured). THIS FILE BECOMES hr_renown_of’s NEW LAST TOUCHER (it had exactly one before, 2026-08-20-renown.sql, and is on no derivation chain); it takes over NO role for hr_credit_kills, which it only patches. ⚠ APPLY ORDER: DEPENDS ON 2026-09-01-kill-daily-credit.sql — §1’s anchor lives in the body THAT file installs, and §0 fails closed BY NAME if it is absent. Ship kill-daily FIRST, faucet SECOND. NO BACKFILL: the credited counters start at zero so renown is UNCHANGED for every existing character at apply time (nobody loses a rank or a perk), and renown already accrued from credited kills since 2026-08-30 is NOT clawed back — the beta is wiped at cutover and hr_claim_rank’s high-water keeps a claimed rank claimed. STATED COST: renown stops scoring attended kills the client credited, a deliberate under-count returning renown to its pre-2026-08-30 position. Server-only: no edge redeploy, no client change, no grant widened, no client call form moved. §3 PROVES on apply, in an HR822-rolled-back subtransaction: the HONEST CONTROL first (a 100-kill settle moves renown by exactly 505, so the fix cannot degenerate into renown-always-0), then the faucet closed (a real accepted bounty + a real hr_credit_kills of 400 on a real is_boss target moves renown by 0, with a fixture-degenerate guard proving the credit actually applied), sustained spam over five re-opened windows still 0, a settle AFTER the credits still scoring (the discount subtracts, it does not latch), the bestiary row still moving and the bounty turn-in still paying. SECURITY PRE-BUILD CONDITIONS FOLDED IN: (1) the two-migration coupling is PINNED, not described — §0a pins TWO hashes, c_expect (the body 2026-09-01 installs, literally that file's own c_self, so the two cannot drift apart about what 'the kill-daily body' means) and c_applied (this file's own output, so a re-apply is a no-op); anything else raises, and applying this file WITHOUT kill-daily fails closed BY NAME with the remedy (verified by booting the chain without it and executing this file). A substring probe was rejected as insufficient because the identical idiom in 2026-09-01 §0b was PROVEN to wave through a hotfix applied on top. (2) RETROACTIVITY is stated rather than implied: forward-only; credited kills since 2026-08-30 keep scoring forever; there is NO backfill source (hr_kill_credit_log is retained two days); already-claimed ranks are unrecoverable (hr_claim_rank consumes a once-per-rank guard and holds a greatest() high-water, so up to 1,603,000 gold + 925 gems per character may already be banked); renownAllXp self-corrects for future credits only. ⚠ AND THE HIGH-WATER IS WORSE THAN 'ranks already taken': an inflated renown_high is also a STANDING CLAIM on every rank BELOW it, because the ratchet does not decay — a score reached once by the faucet keeps every cheaper rank claimable indefinitely, long after this fix stops the score rising that way. Moot today (live max renown_high is 773, below squire's 900), but that is an observation about today's data and not a property, so the trigger is recorded rather than the reassurance. The answer is the BETA WIPE, written down as the whole justification with the explicit trigger that if the wipe is cancelled or deferred past this fix THAT PARAGRAPH must be re-opened, because the correct action becomes a renown recompute plus a rank-claim audit and neither exists. (3) THE ORDERING INVARIANT ev:kill_credited:<id> <= bestiary(<id>) is asserted (the bestiary is written absolutely via greatest, the counter additively). ⚠ The invariant alone proved TOO WEAK to catch its own mutation — honest kills in the bestiary row absorb the overshoot so no inversion appears — so the property that actually holds the line is a SIGNED EQUALITY: a THROTTLED credit must move renown by EXACTLY 0. Above 0 the faucet is open; BELOW 0 the discount is eating renown the player earned honestly, which every 'did not rise' check passes straight over. Asserted at both layers (GATE(c5b) and guard R8); the mutation reads -550. (4) THE CREDITED KEYS CAN NEVER BE PRUNED — period_key='' is the permanent population and hr_progress_prune deletes only period_key <> ''. If a credited row could be swept while the row it discounts survives, the discount fails OPEN and the faucet re-opens on a timer with nothing looking broken. ⚠ THE FIRST PROOF OF THIS WAS VACUOUS (Security C1, caught in the full pass): GATE(c6)/R9 ran the prune at interval '0 seconds' on rows created microseconds earlier, but hr_progress_prune floors its age at greatest(interval '7 days', p_older), so it deleted NOTHING and the assertion passed identically whether the rows were permanent or periodic. Measured: fresh → 0 deleted; backdated 400 days → the periodic control deleted and the credited rows survive. The PROPERTY was true, the PROOF was not testing it. A 'nothing was deleted' assertion is evidence ONLY when something else WAS, so both layers now plant a period_key <> '' CONTROL that must die, age every probe row past the floor, and FAIL THE FIXTURE LOUDLY if the prune reports zero deletions; mutation prune_probe_not_aged restores the vacuous shape and must read RED (it does). (5) READ COST measured, because hr_renown_of is on hr_perks_of's path which the accrual engine calls every settle and the op-count analysis covers WRITES only: both added lookups supply player_progress' complete PRIMARY KEY (one probe for the kill term, one per bestiary row (<=108) for the boss term — no new scan, no new sort). MEASURED ON PRODUCTION against a full bestiary: 2.67 ms/call, a DELTA of +0.44 ms over the undiscounted body (~20% of an already-cheap read, once per ~90s settle). The guard's own ~3 ms figure is a PGlite PROXY, labelled as such in its output, and exists to catch a plan collapsed into a scan per bestiary row (orders of magnitude) rather than to benchmark.
